title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Labor Rate on a Call at a Building Under a Maintenance Agreement
content:
### Points of judgement on the rate a call's labor is billed at

**First.** Where an active preventive maintenance agreement on the account is held at a tier that covers
repair labor and the call was worked at the building that agreement runs at, the demand program bills
nothing for the labor and the rate is nil.

**Second.** Where an active preventive maintenance agreement on the account is held at a tier that does
not cover repair labor, the call was worked at the building that agreement runs at, the tier allows rate
substitution and the agreement's published agreement labor rate is lower than the tier's block overage
rate, that published agreement labor rate is the rate.

**Third.** In any other case no agreement rate takes the place of the program's own rate.

The agreement, the tier it is held at, whether that tier covers repair labor, its published agreement
labor rate and the building it runs at are read from the customer's Preventive Maintenance Agreements
records; the building the call was worked at is read from the completion record of the call.

**The two figures of the Demand Service Rate Programs the conditions turn on** — the block overage rate the agreement rate is
compared against, and whether the program allows a maintenance agreement's labor rate to substitute:

| Program | Block overage rate (USD per hour) | Maintenance agreement labor rate substitutes |
|---|---|---|
| Time & Material Account | 165 | Yes |
| Priority Response Program | 152 | Yes |
| Block Hour Service Program | 144 | Yes |
| Emergency Response Program | 138 | Yes |
| Critical Facility Response Program | 132 | No |
| Dedicated Technician Program | 126 | No |

### The conditions in combination

| Active preventive maintenance agreement on the account | Building | Program allows substitution | Agreement rate against the block overage rate | The rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| held at a tier covering repair labor | the one the agreement runs at | either | either | nil |
| held at a tier covering repair labor | another building | either | either | the program's own rate stands |
| held at a tier not covering repair labor | the one the agreement runs at | yes | lower | the agreement's published labor rate |
| held at a tier not covering repair labor | the one the agreement runs at | yes | at or above | the program's own rate stands |
| held at a tier not covering repair labor | the one the agreement runs at | no | either | the program's own rate stands |
| none active | either | either | either | the program's own rate stands |

On the Critical Facility Response Program and the Dedicated Technician Program the substitution column
stands at No, so an agreement rate of 100 US dollars an hour does not displace their block overage rates
of 132 and 126 US dollars; on the Emergency Response Program, where the column stands at Yes, that same
agreement rate is lower than the block overage rate of 138 US dollars and is the rate.
